Monica / Alex — below is a pragmatic integration guide tailored for Fathom's stated needs. I'll include the Node example inline and attach a fuller sample file (redwood-sdk-sample.js). High-level recommendations first, then code and operational notes.

High-level recommendations (initial rollout):
- Start on hosted multi-tenant endpoint (faster TTV). Switch to Dedicated only if P50 latency or throughput requirements aren't met.
- For bursts up to ~60 rps: enable client-side concurrency limits + token-bucket rate limiter (allow short bursts, cap sustained throughput).
- Recommended timeout: request-level timeout of 10s for generation calls, 30s for long streaming sessions; client TCP keepalive enabled.
- Retry policy: idempotent-ish calls (embeddings, non-streaming) -> up to 3 retries with exponential backoff (base 300ms, factor 2, jitter). For streaming generation, prefer resume/reconnect logic instead of automatic retries.
- Backoff for 429s: immediate small backoff (500ms) then exponential up to 8s; surface 429 headers (x-rate-limit-remaining, x-rate-limit-reset) to clients for adaptive backoff.
- Circuit breaker: trip after 5 consecutive 5xx or 429s in 1 minute; open for 30s then probe.

Node SDK example (streaming + reconnect/backoff):
const Redwood = require('redwood-sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, timeout: 10000 });

async function generateWithRetry(prompt) {
  let attempts = 0;
  const maxRetries = 3;
  while (true) {
    try {
      const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'rw-large-v1', input: prompt, max_tokens: 512 });
      for await (const chunk of stream) {
        process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
      }
      return;
    } catch (err) {
      attempts += 1;
      if (attempts > maxRetries || err.status === 400) throw err;
      // If 429, observe x-rate-limit-reset header when available
      const backoff = Math.min(8000, 300 * Math.pow(2, attempts) + Math.random() * 200);
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, backoff));
    }
  }
}

Operational notes:
- Instrument request-level metrics (latency p50/p95, token consumption) and capture x-rate-limit-* headers for adaptive throttling on your side.
- Use prefix caching (if you have repeated prompts) to reduce token costs; our SDK supports KV cache hooks — we can enable a managed cache if needed.
- Tokenization: estimate tokens using our tokenizer lib before sending large batches; this prevents unexpected 413/413-like failures.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-sample.js (full examples + a small helper for rate-limit header parsing). Also shared a gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/7f3c9a-sample-sdk

Happy to refine after kickoff.

Quick follow-up from engineering regarding retry/timeouts and endpoint migration:
- For endpoint migration: we can provision a customer-scoped API key and a soft-named endpoint (e.g., customer-49821.redwood.ai) for the POC. No infra change required if hosted; Dedicated requires >3-week lead time.
- Concurrency: recommend client max concurrency = 16 simultaneous streams per process for Node app servers; use a pooled worker pattern for larger fleets.
- KV cache note: if Fathom uses short prompts with stable prefixes, enable local LRU + remote KV to avoid repeated prefix compute. This reduces average latency by 20–40% for many customers.
- Timeouts: server-side idle stream timeout is 60s; client-side keepalive at 30s to avoid mid-stream disconnects.

If you expect long synchronous generations >30s, we should instead recommend an async job model (submit -> poll/webhook). We'll discuss tradeoffs on the kickoff.
